focus: A13 install guidance for side-by-side, v1-only and v2-only setups: what must the cli-opencode skill document so a user can copy this repo's setup, or install just one version?
answeredQuestions: What install, verification and pinning guidance supports side-by-side and single-version setups, and which gaps stay irreducible?

label: opencode upgrade on v1 1.19.3 cannot reach 2.x by a plain upgrade: the opencode-ai npm 'latest' dist-tag is 1.19.3 so there is nothing above the installed version, and crossing the major requires the --major flag whose own help text reads 'upgrade to OpenCode 2 and remove OpenCode 1'. The v1 leg of a side-by-side install is therefore upgrade-stable by default and --major must be documented as a destructive migration, never as an upgrade.

v1 and v2 are different npm packages with different bin payloads: opencode-ai@1.19.3 declares bin {opencode} and prints a bare '1.19.3' from --version, while @opencode/cli@2.0.32 declares bin {opencode, opencode2} pointing at one opencode.exe and prints 'opencode v2.0.32'. The second bin name is what makes a non-colliding second copy possible: one install, two entry names, only the non-colliding name placed on PATH. opencode-ai also carries latest-0 and latest-1 dist-tags, per-major latest pointers that keep the 1.x channel from ever resolving a 2.x release.

Homebrew is now a v2-only channel: 'brew info opencode' reports stable 2.0.32, not installed, with versioned_formulae empty and a formula URL under the v2 repository tag; 'brew search opencode' shows no opencode@1. brew therefore cannot participate in a side-by-side setup and, used alone, collides on the opencode name. Document brew as v2-only and exclusive.

The upgrade --method vocabularies diverge between versions: v1 offers curl, npm, pnpm, bun, brew, choco, scoop while v2 offers curl, npm, pnpm, bun, yarn, vp, brew, winget. --log-level diverges too, uppercase DEBUG/INFO/WARN/ERROR on v1 versus lowercase all/trace/debug/info/warn/warning/error/fatal/none on v2. A shared upgrade recipe must omit --method and --log-level or be duplicated per version. Locally available tooling is npm, bun, pnpm, brew and curl; yarn, vp and winget are absent.

The rollback primitives are not interchangeable across versions: v2 'uninstall' is documented as 'Uninstall OpenCode, keeping session data, configuration, and state' with --dry-run and --force, whereas v1's --major upgrade is documented as removing OpenCode 1. Safe rollback is 'opencode2 uninstall --dry-run' then --force on v2 and 'npm uninstall -g --prefix ~/.local opencode-ai' on v1; --major is never a switch, and ~/.config/opencode must never be deleted as cleanup because both versions share it.

The working side-by-side layout is exactly three artifacts: v1 symlinked as ~/.local/bin/opencode into the default npm prefix ~/.local; v2 installed into a second npm prefix ~/.local/opencode-v2 whose bin directory is deliberately absent from PATH so its own opencode cannot shadow v1; and a 260-byte /bin/sh launcher ~/.local/bin/opencode2 that sets OPENCODE_DB=opencode-v2.db before exec. The launcher's own comment states the reason: v2 would otherwise open v1's opencode.db and migrate it in place. The data directory corroborates with three separate databases (opencode.db, opencode-next.db, opencode-v2.db). Both versions still share ~/.config/opencode and the cache, so config isolation is irreducibly absent.

The cli-opencode skill currently contains no install, upgrade or side-by-side guidance at all: a recursive grep for install, curl, side-by-side, OPENCODE_DB and opencode2 over the whole skill tree returns zero hits, and every 'Upgrade' hit is a changelog heading about the skill's own version. A13's output is green-field documentation with nothing existing to reconcile or contradict.

Version detection must be output-shape based, not name based: v1 prints a bare '1.19.3' while v2 prints 'opencode v2.0.32', and on a machine with both installed only the names differ (opencode versus opencode2) whereas on a v2-only machine both names resolve to v2. A detector must probe both names, match ^[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+$ as v1 and a prefixed form as v2, and must not assume a leading v.

A side-by-side install must never place the v2 prefix bin directory on PATH: both package payloads expose a bin named opencode, so the second prefix's bin being off-PATH is the only thing preventing the v2 binary from shadowing v1.
~/.config/opencode is shared by both versions with no per-version override, so any config key written for one version is immediately live on the other.

direction: Reading the v1 compiled binary's strings to settle upgrade or installer behaviour
reason: The v1 binary is a minified bundle with near-unlimited line lengths; a targeted grep returned a 50 KB slice of unrelated TUI code. The --help surface is authoritative for the flag inventory and answered the question directly, so the binary read was dropped rather than retried.

direction: Treating Homebrew as a route to a v1 install
reason: brew info reports stable 2.0.32 with versioned_formulae empty and the formula tracking the v2 repository tag; brew search shows no opencode@1. There is no v1 formula to install.

direction: Pinning v1 by version to prevent drift into 2.x
reason: v1 cannot drift: the opencode-ai latest dist-tag is 1.19.3, the installed version, and crossing the major needs the explicitly destructive --major flag. The channel itself is the pin, so no upgrade-recipe pinning is needed on the v1 leg.
